standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice put-away systems. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: The learner looks at a real, current example of laundry that didn't make it fully into its system — a basket of clean clothes sitting for days, an item in the wrong drawer — and works with an adult to figure out exactly where the system broke down before fixing both the immediate pile and the underlying system.
safetyNotes: No shame language is used toward whoever the pile belongs to.

simulationAlternative.description: If there is no current backlog of unstored laundry to diagnose, the learner instead reviews a short written scenario describing someone else's stalled put-away system, identifies the likely sticking-point step, and proposes a specific fix the same way as the guided task.

materials: learner-local: the actual current pile of clean laundry

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u02-l06-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u02-l06-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u02-l06-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u02-l06-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Explain your updated put-away system in your own words, from clean-and-dry to fully stored, and name the one step you'll watch most closely next time.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u02-l06-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g5-u02-l06-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g5-u02-l06-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Diagnosing the sticking point: Names the specific step where the system stopped. | System adjustment and testing: Proposes and tests one specific change. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u02-l06-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Apply the same diagnose-and-fix process to a different put-away system in the home (dishes, school supplies, toys) and compare whether the same sticking-point step shows up there too.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can practice put-away systems. I will do one step at a time and check one result.

duration.sessionPattern: 5 minutes model, 5–7 minutes guided try, 10–15 minutes learner task, 5 minutes evidence and retry check
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: the actual current pile of clean laundry
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

localMaterials.label: storage furniture (drawers, closet, shelf)
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: put-away systems worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner looks at a real, current example of laundry that didn't make it fully into its system — a basket of clean clothes sitting for days, an item in the wrong drawer — and works with an adult to figure out exactly where the system broke down before fixing both the immediate pile and the underlying system.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact put-away systems decision or action.
Model move 2: Describe the specific put-away problem you're looking at right now — not 'my laundry system doesn't work' but exactly what's out of place.
Model move 3: With your adult, trace back: at what step did this pile stop moving toward its storage spot?
Model check: Diagnosing the sticking point: Names the specific step where the system stopped. | System adjustment and testing: Proposes and tests one specific change.

resources.title: put-away systems action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal for put-away systems.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u02-l06-model-card.
3. Do one coached move on swk-rfl-g5-u02-l06-guided-card.
4. Complete the chosen route on swk-rfl-g5-u02-l06-independent-card.
5. Save the small record on swk-rfl-g5-u02-l06-evidence-record; use swk-rfl-g5-u02-l06-retry-pair if a step is missed.

resources.title: put-away systems coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner looks at a real, current example of laundry that didn't make it fully into its system — a basket of clean clothes sitting for days, an item in the wrong drawer — and works with an adult to figure out exactly where the system broke down before fixing both the immediate pile and the underlying system.
Coach direction: Describe the specific put-away problem you're looking at right now — not 'my laundry system doesn't work' but exactly what's out of place.
Learner prompt: Describe the specific problem.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: put-away systems complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: With your adult, trace back: at what step did this pile stop moving toward its storage spot?
Response 1 (t2-p1): I named the exact step where the system stopped (washed but not folded, folded but not carried to its room, carried but not put in the drawer, etc.).
Response 2 (t2-p2): My adult and I agreed on one specific reason that step is the sticking point.
Response 3 (t2-p3): We named one small change to the system, not just 'try harder.'

Equal-access rule: If there is no current backlog of unstored laundry to diagnose, the learner instead reviews a short written scenario describing someone else's stalled put-away system, identifies the likely sticking-point step, and proposes a specific fix the same way as the guided task.

resources.title: put-away systems minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain your updated put-away system in your own words, from clean-and-dry to fully stored, and name the one step you'll watch most closely next time.
Success checks: Diagnosing the sticking point: Names the specific step where the system stopped. | System adjustment and testing: Proposes and tests one specific change.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: put-away systems supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g5-u02-l06-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g5-u02-l06-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional put-away systems condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Diagnosing the sticking point: Names the specific step where the system stopped. | System adjustment and testing: Proposes and tests one specific change..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u02-l06-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
